title: Guns and Roses Volume. 1
label: Ruff Sqwad Recordings

type.basis: Mixtape CD. A 2020 essay places it in the crew's sample-led romantic phase, but no source ties specific tracks to samples.

sound.text: TRENCH (2020) describes Ruff Sqwad's romantic R&G-era tracks as built over '80s power ballad samples' and made on FruityLoops, naming The Police and Cutting Crew as recognisable sample sources (not specific to this mixtape).

Guardian (Hancox): in 2003-5 the crew's sound grew grander, with synth melodies, sweeping strings and military brass; they chopped rock and classical hooks in FruityLoops and drew on film soundtracks and hip-hop producers like Just Blaze.
sound.pub: c. Dec 2012 (Guardian, Dan Hancox, via inkl)

context.text: Wikipedia: debut mixtape and first of a three-part series; 'considered to be one of the best mixtapes to come from the grime scene' (cited to a record-shop page).
Lyrics by Tinchy Stryder, Dirty Danger, Slix, Rapid and Shifty Rydos.

rels.other: Wiley Kat on 'Wild Clipse'; Trim on 'Jampie'
Ruff Sqwad - Guns and Roses Volume. 2 (2006)

uncertainty: Physical format stated as CD in the Ruff Sqwad Wikipedia article; catalogue number unknown. Trench gives the Collector's Edition date as 1 Feb 2007.
tracklist: 23 tracks incl. 'Jampie' (ft. Trim), 'Wild Clipse' (ft. Wiley Kat), 'Ice Cream' (ft. Roachee), 'Stryder's Back'. Collector's Edition with extra tracks (incl. 'Together') 1 Feb 2007.
